messages:
rachel: FYI I saw a weird pattern on yesterday's canary: three pods in us-west started applying the fallback while the rest stayed on the new variant. It wasn't a full rollback, just local flips. Thinking we need a stability layer at the edge to avoid noisy split decisions. Thoughts? :eyes:

leo: Ugh, saw that too. My rough idea: per-edge short lease (eg 30s) for a local override + a lightweight consensus stamp pushed to telemetry. Lease lets an instance flip quickly and avoid thrashing, stamp gives us post-facto visibility.

deepa: Lease sounds fine but what about churn during scale events? If autoscaler kills pods and new pods come up without the stamp, we'll get oscillation. We should add a hysteresis counter and require N consecutive eval windows before flip-back.

rachel: agree on hysteresis. Also prefer metric smoothing (EWMA) instead of raw p99 spikes. Synthetic probes + a small windowed error-count seems most stable.

leo: concrete sketch:
- edge evaluates: combine EWMA(probe_error_rate) and EWMA(p99_latency)
- if combined_score > threshold => set local_override with TTL=25s
- override includes reason code and sample_id stamped to central telemetry
- when override set, start backoff: 25s -> 50s -> 100s before allowing immediate re-eval
- require 3 consecutive healthy windows (configurable) before removing override

rachel: Love the backoff ladder. We should guard against per-tenant extremes: add a per-tenant rate cap so a noisy tenant can't flip whole node. Maybe override only applies to traffic for that tenant unless node-level probes show cluster-wide issues.

ops-bot: [alert] canary-fallback: instance i-0b123 triggered local_override (reason: probe_error_rate) at 2025-08-02T14:02:13Z

deepa: Operational boundaries: who owns the probe sources? infra can own generic synthetic probes and latency collection; runtime should surface feature-specific detectors (e.g., hallucination checks). Edge policy should accept both signals and apply weighting.

leo: For consistency w/ Dedicated/Private: policy config should be versioned and backwards compatible, support optional central-forcing keys (operator breakglass), and be pluggable so private control-plane can push same semantics.

rachel: Example policy blob (simple, for implementation):
```json
{
  "schema": "edge-fallback-v2",
  "apply_scope": "tenant|node",
  "scores": {
    "probe_error_ewma": {"threshold": 0.04, "alpha": 0.2, "window_s": 30},
    "p99_latency_ewma_ms": {"threshold": 900, "alpha": 0.15, "window_s": 60}
  },
  "consecutive_windows_to_recover": 3,
  "override_ttl_s": 25,
  "backoff_sequence_s": [25,50,100],
  "operator_force_key": "console.override.v1"
}
```
(we'll pick exact numbers in config review)

leo: One more safety: when a node flips to fallback we should tag traces with header: x-edge-fallback: instance-id=..., reason=..., policy_rev=... so SRE can slice traces. Also emit metric edged_override_count{reason, tenant}.

deepa: Perf consideration: decision path must be cheap. Do eval after probe aggregation tick, not per-request. Decision stores ephemeral state in memory; don't persist to disk.

rachel: Decisions / action items:
1) leo to prototype a minimal config & evaluation loop (PR) -- this week.
2) infra to own synthetic probes and EWMA library, publish recommended alphas/thresholds -- next week.
3) runtime to add feature detectors and map signal weightings into policy -- next sprint.
4) SRE to add trace header + metrics instrumentation plan -- rachel will coordinate.

leo: Open question: central arbitration for long-lived disputes? My vote: keep local-first for speed, but a central reconciler can detect nodes that keep flipping and trigger operator alerts / automated central override if widespread.

rachel: ok. We'll aim local-first + central-watchdog. If widespread, central can force node-level overrides via operator_force_key.

ops-bot: [deploy-check] edge-policy schema v2 validated against CI. 1 info: consider exposing "min_evaluate_interval_s" for high-churn clusters.

deepa: I'll draft a short doc on evaluation cadence, EWMA defaults, and tenant isolation rules. rachel, can you own compatibility notes for Dedicated?

rachel: Yep. I'll draft compatibility notes and keep the schema forward-compatible.
